1.s: Paul is astonished that the Galatians are turning to “a different gospel”. His gospel came by revelation of Jesus Christ, not from people.
1.d: Paul skips his usual thanksgiving, showing how urgent the matter is. He tells his conversion and early years.

2.s: The Jerusalem leaders accepted Paul’s mission to Gentiles. Paul opposed Peter in Antioch for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles. “I have been crucified with Christ… Christ lives in me.”
2.d: “A man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ.”

3.s: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by faith? Abraham believed God. Christ became a curse for us. “There is neither Jew nor Greek… neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.”
3.d: 3:28 has been called a charter of equality in the church.

4.s: God sent his Son “when the fullness of the time came” so we might be adopted as children, crying “Abba, Father!” The allegory of Hagar and Sarah.
4.d: The law was a guardian until Christ came.

5.s: “Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free” Use freedom to serve one another in love. Walk by the Spirit: “the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control.”
5.d: The fruit (singular) of the Spirit is contrasted with the works of the flesh.

6.s: Bear one another’s burdens. “Whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.” Paul writes in large letters with his own hand: “a new creation” is what matters.
6.d: Paul glories only in the cross of Christ.
